newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares race to new highs on Dow strength.
newsitem.headline: German shares race to new highs on Dow strength.

text.p: Germany's DAX index, which measures trade in 30 blue-chip German shares, opened bourse dealings on Tuesday at an all-time record high after a strong overnight close on Wall Street, a firmer dollar and bond gains.
German shares opened bourse trade at 2,711.22 and then continued to rally. After under an hour of floor dealings, the DAX was up 30.03 points, or 1.11 percent, at 2,723.91 points.
The Dow Jones Industrial index ended Monday's trade on Wall Street at 6,010 points, the first close above the 6,000-point level, seen as important for market sentiment.

The strong U.S. close combined with the ongoing strength of the dollar and German bonds helped the German index to open bourse trade comfortably above its own psychologically-important 2,700-point marker.
"Everything is really positive," said one trader, "It's not just the Dow, people are generally positive on the DAX and we've been consolidating for a few days."
The DAX reached new record highs early last week, but had then taken a breather below the 2,700 point mark, with dealers saying the market needed time to consolidate.

Dealers said Western European car registration figures out after the end of trade on Monday had given a boost to auto stocks. Car manufacturer Daimler Benz in particular benefitted from the news, adding 2.03 marks to trade at 85.95.
They also said positive nine-month sales figures from Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG was supporting the German chemicals sector.
Among the medium-sized stocks, Gehe gained 4.8 marks to 112.50 after it said it would sell its pharmaceutical production units for around 1.2 billion marks.
Troubled German engineering group, Deutsch Babcock, which slipped to a year low on Monday, recovered some ground to trade up 2.80 marks at 50.20.
